tip: домой (damoy = homeward) is the motion form for heading home; дома (doma) would mean being at home with no movement.
так... что (tak... chto = so... that) ties a degree to its result: так быстро (tak bystra = so fast) that понять (panyat) is hard.
для того чтобы (dlya tavo chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive states purpose: получить (paluchit = to get) a visa.
успеть на (uspet na) takes accusative and means make it in time for: успели на поезд (uspeli na poezd = made the train).
дело в том, что (dela v tom, chto = the thing is that) is a fixed frame for introducing the real explanation.
Unreal past conditions use если бы (esli by) plus a past verb, then бы (by) again in the result: знал (znal = knew), пришёл (prishyol = came).
давай (davay) plus a perfective we-form makes a suggestion: давай сходим (davay skhodim = let us go).
желаю (zhelayu = I wish) takes the genitive of what you wish: приятного вечера (priyatnava vechera = a pleasant evening).
едва... как (edva... kak = barely... when) links one action to the next that follows right after: закончил (zakonchil = finished), then раздался (razdalsya = rang).
вместо того чтобы (vmesta tavo chtoby = instead of) plus an infinitive: учиться (uchitsya = to study) rather than doing something else.
Paired ни... ни (ni... ni = neither... nor) still keeps не on the verb: не знали (ne znali = did not know).
в то время как (v to vremya kak = while) plus imperfectives shows two actions running at once: работал (rabotal), готовила (gatovila).
The -ся (-sya) ending makes соблюдается (sablyudaetsya = is observed) passive: the tradition gets kept, with no actor named.
кто бы ни (kto by ni = whoever) plus a past verb means no matter who: пришёл (prishyol = came), everyone was glad.
сказав (skazav = having said) is a verbal adverb for a second action by one subject; не сказав (ne skazav) means without saying.
For a reported yes/no question, put ли (li = whether) right after the verb: могу ли (magu li = whether I can).
будьте любезны (budte lyubezny = be so kind) plus an infinitive like передать (peredat = to pass) makes a formal polite request.
так (tak = so) paired with что (chto = that) links a degree to a result, as in так рад, что (tak rad, chto = so glad that).
In до тех пор пока ... не (do tekh por paka ... ne = until), the final не (ne) is not a real negation: не позвонит (ne pazvanit) marks until he calls.
After a comparative like умнее (umnee = smarter), чем (chem = than) introduces the comparison.
как бы ни (kak by ni = no matter how) sets up a concession: как бы ни было трудно (kak by ni byla trudna = no matter how hard).
с тех пор как (s tekh por kak = since) marks a starting point in time, unlike так как (tak kak = because) which gives a reason.
Paired comparatives use the frame чем больше ..., тем больше (chem bolshe ..., tem bolshe = the more ..., the more).
не только ..., но и (ne tolka ..., no i = not only ..., but also) is a fixed correlative pair joining two facts about one subject.
чтобы (chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive shows purpose: чтобы помочь (chtoby pamoch = in order to help).
в том (v tom) literally means in that; it is a fixed frame pointing ahead to the clause after the comma, as in вопрос в том (vapros v tom = the question is).
пока не (paka ne) here means until; the не carries no negation, so стемнело (stemnela = got dark) still happened.
без (bez = without) always forces the genitive case, which is why kind people appears as добрых людей (dobryh lyudej).
как только (kak tolka) means as soon as; Russian uses the future here, сможет (smozhet = will be able), where English says could.
пока (paka) with no не (ne) means while, two things happening at once: пока мы ехали (paka my ehali = while we drove).
